THE DECK DID NOT SHIP. Five scoring rounds, panel median 6.552 against a 6.8 bar, and one hard fail. A hard fail stops the deck at any round whatever the median is.
The hard fail was NOT repaired, deliberately. A run that fixes a fault after the final round and then ships has graded its own repair. The branch carries the deck the panel actually read.
No merge. The pull request is open and ready and carries everything.

No variety ledger entries, because those exist to constrain the next deck against what shipped. AN ARTICLE PAGE WAS PUBLISHED ANYWAY and an earlier draft of this line said it was not. site_build.py writes one for any date with run artifacts and site_fresh_check then forbids deleting it, so a run cannot opt out of publishing a deck it just refused to ship. Nothing reaches the live site only because the branch does not merge, which is a rule about git rather than about the page. Merging this branch for the record work would publish it.
